title: Appropriate grant award of $207,411 for speed racing street takeover
synopsis: Accepts and spends a $207,411 grant to address street takeovers and speed racing.

title: Amend Fire Regulations Code to adopt current Oregon Fire Code with City amendments (amend Code Title 31)
synopsis: Updates the City's fire code to adopt the current Oregon Fire Code, with Portland-specific amendments.

title: Consent to franchise transfer from Zenith Energy Terminals Holdings LLC to ISQ Springer Holdings, LLC (amend Ordinance 188554)
synopsis: Would have approved transferring the Zenith Energy terminal franchise to a new owner, ISQ Springer Holdings. It failed; a motion to reconsider was pending as of Sept 23, 2026.

title: Urge the City Administrator to refrain from signing data center non-disclosure agreements, notify City Council of inquiries for data center deals, and engage in transparent public processes related to data centers
synopsis: Urges the City Administrator not to sign non-disclosure agreements with data center developers, to tell Council about data center inquiries, and to handle any data center deals through open public processes.

title: Appropriate grant award of $35 million for Section 108 Loan Guarantee Program
synopsis: Accepts $35 million under the federal Section 108 Loan Guarantee Program.

title: Authorize exception to Code Chapter 17.93 Renaming City Streets and authorize the renaming of Cesar E. Chavez Blvd to Campesinos Blvd (allow exceptions to Code Sections 17.93.010, 17.93.020, 17.93.030, 17.93.040 and 17.93.050)
synopsis: Renames Cesar E. Chavez Blvd to Campesinos Blvd, making an exception to the City's usual street-renaming rules.

title: Accept the Future of Large-Scale Performing Arts recommendations to advance a new Broadway-capable venue as part of the proposed Performing Arts + Culture Center at Portland State University, and initiate planning for the future of the Keller Auditorium
synopsis: Accepts recommendations to pursue a new Broadway-capable venue in the proposed Performing Arts + Culture Center at Portland State University and to start planning the Keller Auditorium's future.

title: Authorize an increase up to $245,000 in bureau rates for FY 2026-27 to implement a pilot program to subsidize transit passes for City employees
synopsis: Raises bureau rates by up to $245,000 this fiscal year to fund a pilot that subsidizes transit passes for City employees.

title: Direct the City Administrator to advance a process to identify a development partner for City-owned properties adjacent to the Moda Center
synopsis: Directs the City Administrator to start looking for a development partner for City-owned land next to the Moda Center.

title: Amend the Comprehensive Plan Map and Zoning Map for a vacant lot on NW 31st Ave described as Willamette Heights Addition, Block 18, Lot 14 at the request of Portland Parks and Recreation (LU 26-007966 CP ZC)
synopsis: Changes the Comprehensive Plan and zoning map designations for a vacant lot on NW 31st Ave, at Portland Parks & Recreation's request.

title: Direct the Portland Bureau of Transportation to evaluate and implement no turn on red restrictions at signalized intersections within the High Crash Network
synopsis: Directs the Bureau of Transportation to study and put in place no-turn-on-red restrictions at signalized intersections on the High Crash Network.

title: Authorize a non-binding term sheet with Rip City Management LLC and Trail Blazers Holdings, LLC outlining the terms for Moda Center arena renovation, operating and lease agreements that will keep the Portland Trail Blazers playing in Portland for at least 20 more years
synopsis: Approves a non-binding term sheet with the Trail Blazers' ownership for Moda Center renovation, operating and lease agreements meant to keep the team in Portland for at least 20 more years.

title: ​​Amend City Code and improve land use regulations through the Regulatory Improvement Code Amendment Package 11 (amend Code Titles 32 and 33)​
synopsis: Package 11 of the Regulatory Improvement Code Amendment Package: a batch of fixes and clarifications to the City's land use and building regulations.

title: Consider appeals of the Design Commission’s approval of a voluntary Central City Master Plan Review and Adjustment Review for the Lloyd Center Central City Master Plan (LU 25-091308 CCMS AD)
synopsis: Council's decision on appeals of the Design Commission's approval of the Lloyd Center Central City Master Plan; this vote adopted Council's written findings.

title: Amend Partial and Full Exemptions of System Development Charges for Affordable Housing Developments Code to temporarily remove income requirements for homeownership units (amend Code Section 30.01.095)
synopsis: Temporarily removes income limits for homeownership units that qualify for affordable-housing exemptions from System Development Charges.

title: Add Electric Vehicle Charging Systems Funding Code (add Code Chapter 26.11)
synopsis: Adds a City code chapter setting up funding for electric vehicle charging systems.

title: Authorize a five-year lease with American Property Management for Community Safety Division eastside office
synopsis: Approves a five-year lease for an eastside office for the Community Safety Division.

title: Amend the FY 2026-27 Budget to appropriate $13,076,892 in Portland Clean Energy Fund interest income, $5,491,002 other fund resources, and $335,000 in County IGA revenues to restore frontline positions and services reduced in the approved budget and to provide transition support for affected employees
synopsis: Would have amended the FY 2026-27 budget to spend about $13.1 million in Portland Clean Energy Fund interest, plus about $5.8 million in other funds, to restore frontline positions and services cut in the approved budget and to support affected employees. Councilors split 6-6; Mayor Wilson broke the tie by voting Nay.

title: Adopt a Supplemental Budget for FY 2026-27 to reduce potential risks to City services
synopsis: Adopts a supplemental budget for FY 2026-27 intended to reduce risks to City services.

title: Amend Vehicles and Traffic Code to clarify applicability of ride fees and establish a Drivers’ Resource Center for Transportation Network Company drivers (amend Code Sections 16.40.030 and 16.40.240)
synopsis: Clarifies which rides the City's ride fees apply to and creates a Drivers' Resource Center for rideshare (Uber, Lyft and similar) drivers.

title: Direct the City Administrator to reestablish a Permitting Improvement Team to lead the second phase of the Code Alignment Project
synopsis: Directs the City Administrator to bring back a Permitting Improvement Team to lead the second phase of the Code Alignment Project.

title: Establish 2026 sale price cap for the Homebuyer Opportunity Limited Tax Exemption Program​
synopsis: Sets the 2026 maximum sale price for homes in the Homebuyer Opportunity Limited Tax Exemption program.

title: Revise sewer and stormwater rates, charges, and fees for FY 2026-27
synopsis: Sets sewer and stormwater rates, charges and fees for FY 2026-27.

title: Authorize a Cable Franchise Fund for the Bureau of Planning and Sustainability to support the collection of Public, Education, and Government revenues and manage cable franchise work related to intergovernmental agreements with jurisdictions
synopsis: Creates a Cable Franchise Fund in the Bureau of Planning and Sustainability to collect public, education and government channel revenue and manage cable franchise work with other jurisdictions.

title: Amend City Code to reflect the dissolution of the Mt. Hood Cable Regulatory Commission​ (amend Code Chapters 3.33 and 3.115)
synopsis: Updates City code to reflect that the Mt. Hood Cable Regulatory Commission has been dissolved.

title: Amend City Code to transfer oversight of portable sign placement in the right of way and remove registration requirements (amend Code Title 32 and add Code Chapter 17.110)
synopsis: Moves oversight of portable signs placed in the public right of way to a new code chapter and drops the registration requirement.

title: Adopt the annual budget of the City and establish appropriations for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027
synopsis: Adopts the City's annual budget and spending authority for FY 2026-27.

title: Approve levying taxes for the City for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027
synopsis: Levies the City's property taxes for FY 2026-27.

title: Adopt the Supplemental Budget for the FY 2025-26 over-expenditure process and make budget adjustments in various funds
synopsis: Supplemental budget for FY 2025-26 covering over-expenditures and adjustments across City funds.

title: Authorize sewer revenue bonds to finance sewer system capital improvements for an amount sufficient to produce net proceeds of up to $235 million and to refund outstanding sewer revenue bonds
synopsis: Authorizes sewer revenue bonds for up to $235 million in net proceeds for sewer system improvements, and to refinance existing sewer bonds.

title: Adopt and implement the Moderate-Income Revolving Loan Program
synopsis: Creates and launches the Moderate-Income Revolving Loan Program, run by Prosper Portland.

title: Authorize the Bureau of Transportation to acquire certain permanent and temporary property rights necessary for the construction of the 174th Sidewalk Infill Kelly to Francis streets, SE Project, through the exercise of the City’s eminent domain authority
synopsis: Authorizes the Bureau of Transportation to use eminent domain to acquire property rights for a sidewalk infill project on SE 174th Ave between Kelly and Francis streets.

title: Approve the designation of twelve trees as City Heritage Trees and remove the City Heritage Tree designation from fourteen trees
synopsis: Designates twelve trees as City Heritage Trees and removes that designation from fourteen others.

title: Amend Portland Permitting & Development Fee Schedules to improve cost recovery to ensure an adequate level of service
synopsis: Raises Portland Permitting & Development fees to recover more of the cost of providing permit services.

title: Appropriate $2,500,000 from the Construction Excise Tax Sub-fund 225020 for homeownership development in District 2
synopsis: Spends $2.5 million from the Construction Excise Tax fund on homeownership development in District 2.

title: Create a Sister City relationship between the City of Portland and the City of Lviv, Ukraine
synopsis: Makes Lviv, Ukraine, a Portland sister city.

title: Add Code to prohibit the sale or provision of certain force-fed poultry products (add Code Chapter 17.110)
synopsis: Bans selling or providing certain force-fed poultry products, such as foie gras, in Portland.

title: Amend Portland Clean Energy Community Benefits Fund Code to allow a transfer of interest earned in FY 2024-25 for the FY 2026-27 budget (amend Code Section 7.07.060)
synopsis: Changes the Portland Clean Energy Fund code so interest earned in FY 2024-25 can be moved into the FY 2026-27 budget.

title: Adopt solid waste and recycling rates and fees for franchised residential collection and the commercial tonnage fee, effective July 1, 2026 (amend ENN-2.09)
synopsis: Sets garbage and recycling rates for residential collection and the commercial tonnage fee, starting July 1, 2026.

title: Revise transportation fees, rates and charges for FY 2026-27 and amend Transportation Fee Schedule (amend TRN 3.450)
synopsis: Updates transportation fees, rates and charges for FY 2026-27.

title: Revise sewer and stormwater rates, charges and fees for FY 2026-27
synopsis: Updates sewer and stormwater rates, charges and fees for FY 2026-27.

title: Adopt rates, charges, and fees for water and water-related services for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, and ending June 30, 2027 (amend ADM-14.07)
synopsis: Sets water rates, charges and fees for FY 2026-27.

title: Add Identification of Law Enforcement Officers Code to prohibit facial covering, require badge visibility, and require identity verification for individuals conducting law enforcement activities (add Code Chapter 23.30)
synopsis: Bars people doing law enforcement work in Portland from covering their faces, and requires them to show a badge and verify their identity.

title: Amend Arts Tax Code to provide tax relief, promote sustainability of Arts Access Fund, define critical terms, and respond to community and audit recommendations (amend Code Chapter 6.10)
synopsis: Changes the Arts Tax to provide tax relief, keep the Arts Access Fund sustainable, define key terms, and respond to community and audit recommendations.

title: Authorize water revenue bonds to finance water system capital improvements for an amount sufficient to produce net proceeds of up to $525,000,000 and to refund outstanding water revenue bonds
synopsis: Authorizes water revenue bonds for up to $525 million in net proceeds for water system improvements, and to refinance existing water bonds.

title: Consider appeal by Pleasant Valley Neighborhood Association against the Hearings Officer’s decision to approve with conditions a Planned Development, Land Division and Environmental Review for the creation of 12 single-dwelling lots and 1 multi-dwelling lot in the Pleasant Valley Neighborhood (LU 23-003731 LDS EN PD)
synopsis: Council's decision on the Pleasant Valley Neighborhood Association's appeal of a Hearings Officer approval for a development of 12 single-dwelling lots and one multi-dwelling lot; this vote adopted Council's written findings.

title: Approve funding recommendations of the Portland Children’s Levy Allocation Committee for July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2029
synopsis: Approves the Portland Children's Levy Allocation Committee's funding recommendations for July 2026 through June 2029.

title: Authorize borrowings of not more than $95 million in anticipation of the Fire and Police Disability and Retirement Fund levy for FY 2026-27
synopsis: Allows the City to borrow up to $95 million ahead of collecting the Fire and Police Disability and Retirement Fund levy for FY 2026-27.

title: Authorize conveyance of City-owned real property to Habitat for Humanity Portland/Metro East for the construction of True North project
synopsis: Transfers City-owned land to Habitat for Humanity Portland/Metro East to build the True North project.

title: Amend Chronic Nuisance Property Code to address human trafficking, gun violence, and administrative challenges (amend Code Chapter 14B.60)
synopsis: Updates the Chronic Nuisance Property code to address human trafficking, gun violence and administrative problems.

title: Authorize the Bureau of Transportation to acquire certain permanent property rights necessary for a replacement rockfall mitigation system for the W Burnside Road – SW Tichner Drive Slide Project, through the exercise of the City’s eminent domain authority
synopsis: Authorizes the Bureau of Transportation to use eminent domain to acquire property rights for a replacement rockfall barrier on the W Burnside Road – SW Tichner Drive slide project.

title: Establish a new Transportation Utility Fee to help fund basic maintenance and safety of the City’s transportation system (add Code Chapter 17.20)
synopsis: Creates a new Transportation Utility Fee to help pay for basic maintenance and safety of Portland's streets.

title: Amend franchise granted to Comcast of Oregon II, Inc. to reflect the dissolution of the Mt. Hood Cable Regulatory Commission (amend Ordinance 192084)​
synopsis: Amends Comcast's cable franchise to reflect that the Mt. Hood Cable Regulatory Commission has been dissolved.

title: Support modification of Bureau of Transportation street opening permits to utilities to include damage cost recovery related to long-term pavement degradation associated with excavation in the public right-of-way
synopsis: Supports changing street-opening permits so utilities that dig up the public right-of-way pay for the long-term pavement damage it causes.

title: Adopt the FY 2025-26 Technical Adjustment Ordinance and make other budget-related changes
synopsis: Makes technical adjustments and other budget changes to the FY 2025-26 budget.

title: Direct City Administrator to develop accelerated timeline for the Inner Eastside Area Planning Project and identify future area planning and zoning actions to advance housing production goals
synopsis: Directs the City Administrator to speed up the Inner Eastside Area Planning Project and identify future planning and zoning steps to boost housing production.

title: Add Code to establish the Portland Committee on Community-Engaged Policing (add Code Chapter 3.23)
synopsis: Creates the Portland Committee on Community-Engaged Policing in City code.

title: Vacate NE Couch St and NE Davis St west of NE 97th Ave subject to certain conditions and reservations (VAC-10140)
synopsis: Vacates (removes from public right-of-way) sections of NE Couch St and NE Davis St west of NE 97th Ave, with conditions.

title: Amend Business License Law Code to increase the business license tax gross receipts exemption (amend Code Section 7.02.400)
synopsis: Raises the gross-receipts threshold below which businesses are exempt from the City business license tax.

title: Authorize a temporary interfund loan not to exceed $15 million from the Facilities Services Fund to the Health Insurance Operating Fund to provide interim funding for employee health benefits and to avoid negative cash and fund balances at the end of FY 2025-26
synopsis: Allows a temporary loan of up to $15 million from the Facilities Services Fund to cover employee health benefits and avoid a negative balance at the end of FY 2025-26.

title: Amend Office of the City Attorney Code to authorize payment of costs for City employees facing certain criminal or civil proceedings (amend Code Section 3.10.020)
synopsis: Lets the City pay certain legal costs for City employees facing some criminal or civil proceedings.

title: Amend Campaign Finance Code to maintain enforcement of voter-approved regulations following court order (amend Code Chapter 2.10)
synopsis: Updates the Campaign Finance code so the City can keep enforcing voter-approved campaign finance rules after a court order.

title: ​​Adopt the Public Infrastructure Environmental Code Project to streamline environmental zoning regulations to accommodate needed infrastructure projects and support ongoing natural resource management (amend Code Title 33)​
synopsis: Adopts the Public Infrastructure Environmental Code Project, streamlining environmental zoning rules so needed infrastructure projects can be built while natural resources continue to be managed.

title: ​​Amend Civil Rights Code related to sexual orientation and family status definitions and amend nondiscrimination clauses (amend Code Section 14A.50.110 and Code Chapter 23.01)
synopsis: Updates the City's Civil Rights code definitions of sexual orientation and family status and revises nondiscrimination clauses.

title: ​​Declare the City of Portland will defend the rights of transgender people and all of the LGBTQIA2S+ community​
synopsis: Declares that the City will defend the rights of transgender people and the wider LGBTQIA2S+ community.

title: Amend the Portland Clean Energy Community Benefit Fund Climate Investment Plan​
synopsis: Amends the Portland Clean Energy Community Benefits Fund's Climate Investment Plan.

title: ​​Approve the Cully Tax Increment Financing District Five-Year Action Plan
synopsis: Approves the five-year action plan for the Cully Tax Increment Financing District.

title: Authorize Bureau of Transportation to acquire certain permanent and temporary property rights necessary for construction of the NE MLK Blvd Safety and Access to Transit Project, through the exercise of the City’s eminent domain authority
synopsis: Authorizes the Bureau of Transportation to use eminent domain to acquire property rights for the NE MLK Blvd Safety and Access to Transit Project.

title: Amend the FY 2025–26 Appropriation Schedule to reallocate $150,000 from the Legal Priorities Reserve Fund to support refugee and immigration legal services
synopsis: Moves $150,000 from the Legal Priorities Reserve Fund to refugee and immigration legal services.

title: Accept the Supporting Portland’s Storefronts Report to establish a Storefront Support Program
synopsis: Accepts the Supporting Portland's Storefronts report and sets up a Storefront Support Program.

title: ​​Adopt the Affordable Housing Opportunities Project amendments to the Comprehensive Plan Map and the Official Zoning Map
synopsis: Adopts the Affordable Housing Opportunities Project's changes to the Comprehensive Plan Map and zoning map.

title: Amend Council Committee Code to allow for the creation of a Council Committee of the Whole (amend Code Section 3.02.050)
synopsis: Changes the Council Committee code to allow a Council Committee of the Whole.

title: Commemorate the life of George Floyd and reaffirm the commitment to racial justice of the City of Portland
synopsis: Commemorates George Floyd and reaffirms the City's commitment to racial justice.

title: Authorize submission of a minor boundary change request to the State of Oregon to amend the Portland Enterprise Zone boundary
synopsis: Asks the State of Oregon for a minor change to the boundary of the Portland Enterprise Zone.

title: Declare bridge between SE 17th Ave and SE 26th Ave to be named Brooklyn Bridge and direct the City Administrator to authorize update of signage as appropriate
synopsis: Names the bridge between SE 17th and SE 26th avenues the Brooklyn Bridge and directs updated signage.

title: Establish new City Council committees
synopsis: Creates new City Council committees.

title: Add Nondiscrimination Requirements for Single-Occupant Restrooms in Places of Public Accommodation Code to establish equal restroom access by requiring gender neutral signage (add Code Section 23.01.071)
synopsis: Requires single-occupant restrooms in places open to the public to have gender-neutral signage, so everyone has equal access.

title: Add Appointed Boards, Commissions and Committees Code (add Code Chapter 3.40)
synopsis: Adds a City code chapter governing the City's appointed boards, commissions and committees.

title: Appoint members to the Community Board for Police Accountability
synopsis: Appoints members to the Community Board for Police Accountability.

title: Require Deputy City Administrator for Public Safety to provide a report on police officer recruitment goals and costs
synopsis: Requires the Deputy City Administrator for Public Safety to report on police officer recruitment goals and their costs.

title: Amend Renaming City Streets Code to realign with Oregon Revised Statute 227.120 by redelegating decision-making authority to City Council to approve or deny street renaming proposals (amend Code Chapter 17.93)
synopsis: Gives City Council, rather than staff, the power to approve or deny street renaming proposals, matching state law.

title: ​​Amend Portland Clean Energy Community Benefits Code to allow a transfer of interest earned in FY 2023-24 for the FY 2025-26 budget (amend Code Section 7.07.060)​
synopsis: Changes the Portland Clean Energy Fund code so interest earned in FY 2023-24 can be used in the FY 2025-26 budget.

title: Exempt certain code requirements under City Code Chapter 17.93 Renaming City Streets for the proposed renaming of a portion of SW Jackson Street to SW Rose Hill Street
synopsis: Makes exceptions to the street-renaming rules for a proposal to rename part of SW Jackson Street to SW Rose Hill Street.

title: Require City Administrator to release public records in reference to unspent surplus funds and schedule an oversight hearing
synopsis: Requires the City Administrator to release public records about unspent surplus funds and schedules an oversight hearing.

title: Add Code to establish a City Data and Privacy Office (add Code Chapter 3.39)
synopsis: Creates a City Data and Privacy Office in City code.

title: Direct the City Administrator to establish a City Data and Privacy Office to advance privacy protections, steward data assets, and minimize risks from data brokers, uncontrolled sharing of personal information, and secondary data use
synopsis: Directs the City Administrator to set up a City Data and Privacy Office to strengthen privacy protections, manage City data, and reduce risks from data brokers and uncontrolled sharing of personal information.

title: Transmit report to the City on Portland Police Bureau Officer-Involved Shootings and Critical Incidents by the OIR Group
synopsis: Receives the OIR Group's report on Portland Police Bureau officer-involved shootings and critical incidents.

title: Pay settlement of Eric Heard employment discrimination lawsuit in the sum of $75,000 involving Portland Fire & Rescue
synopsis: Pays $75,000 to settle an employment discrimination lawsuit involving Portland Fire & Rescue.

title: Pay Settlement of Stellar J Corporation Contract Claims in the Amount of $650,000
synopsis: Pays $650,000 to settle Stellar J Corporation's contract claims against the City.

title: Approve Plan of Action as required by the Oregon Secretary of State to finding by outside auditors of material weaknesses in the FY 2024-25 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report
synopsis: Approves the plan of action required by the Oregon Secretary of State after outside auditors found material weaknesses in the City's FY 2024-25 annual financial report.

title: Establish a Portland City Council Governance Handbook to collect policies, procedures, and current practices to support City operations and improve transparency
synopsis: Creates a Portland City Council Governance Handbook collecting Council's policies, procedures and practices, to support City operations and transparency.

title: Adopt Homelessness Response System Action Plan and Key Performance Indicators
synopsis: Adopts the Homelessness Response System Action Plan and the measures used to track its performance.

title: Adopt the 2026 State and Federal Legislative Agendas
synopsis: Adopts the City's 2026 state and federal legislative agendas.

title: Request the City Budget Office provide balanced program offer information for Portland Parks & Recreation as pilot project for FY 2026-27 budget
synopsis: Asks the City Budget Office to present Portland Parks & Recreation's FY 2026-27 budget as balanced program offers, as a pilot.

title: Adopt procedure for annual Council strategic priority setting
synopsis: Sets a procedure for Council to set its strategic priorities each year.

title: Appoint Raymond C. Lee III as City Administrator
synopsis: Appoints Raymond C. Lee III as City Administrator, the City's top appointed executive.

title: Certify abstract of votes cast and proclaim Measure 26-260 approved at the Municipal Nonpartisan Special Election held on November 4, 2025
synopsis: Certifies the vote count and declares Measure 26-260 approved in the Nov. 4, 2025 special election.

title: Ratify a successor collective bargaining agreement with American Federation of State, County, Municipal Employees, Local 189, for represented employees within the Office of Independent Police Review for the terms and conditions of employment of represented employees in the Independent Police Review bargaining unit
synopsis: Ratifies a new labor contract with AFSCME Local 189 for represented employees in the Office of Independent Police Review.

title: Require City Administrator to prepare a report with recommendations to reform the City design review process
synopsis: Requires the City Administrator to report with recommendations for reforming the City's design review process.

title: Amend Protests and Appeals and Revenue Division Appeals Board Code (amend Code Sections 7.02.290 and 7.02.295)
synopsis: Updates the code on tax protests and appeals and on the Revenue Division Appeals Board.

title: Amend Special Taxes Code to conform to Oregon Revised Statute 314.835 (amend Code Sections 6.04.130, 6.05.070, 6.09.040, and add Code Section 6.04.135)
synopsis: Updates the City's special taxes code to conform with state law (ORS 314.835).

title: Amend Lloyd Business District Fee Code to correct inadvertent change (amend Code Sections 6.06.260 and 6.06.270)
synopsis: Corrects an unintended change to the Lloyd Business District fee code.

title: Add Detention Facility Impact Fee Code to ensure fair cost sharing in high-impact land uses and to reduce burden on Portland taxpayers (add Code Chapter 5.80)
synopsis: Creates a Detention Facility Impact Fee so high-impact land uses such as detention facilities share more of their public costs.

title: Amend Business License Law Code to allow sharing select business license tax information with the Bureau of Environmental Services (amend Code Section 7.02.240)
synopsis: Allows the City to share selected business license tax information with the Bureau of Environmental Services.

title: Declare City property located at 1436 SE Spokane St, known as the Sellwood Community Center, as surplus property and authorize City Administrator to dispose of the property by sale to Friends of Sellwood Community House​
synopsis: Declares the Sellwood Community Center (1436 SE Spokane St) surplus and authorizes its sale to Friends of Sellwood Community House.

title: Adopt City of Portland Investment Policy
synopsis: Adopts the City of Portland's investment policy.

title: Amend Affordable Housing Code to add prohibition of anti-competitive rental practices including the sale and use of algorithmic devices (add Code Section 30.01.088)
synopsis: Bans anti-competitive rental practices, including selling or using algorithmic rent-setting software.

title: Adopt the FY 2025-26 Fall Supplemental Budget and make other budget related changes
synopsis: Adopts the FY 2025-26 fall supplemental budget and other budget changes.

title: Authorize revenue bonds in an amount sufficient to provide not more than $41 million to finance City fleet maintenance facility improvements and related costs
synopsis: Authorizes up to $41 million in revenue bonds for improvements to the City's fleet maintenance facilities.

title: Authorize the City to acquire certain permanent and temporary property rights necessary for construction of the 3260 SW Upper Drive north to 3139 SW Upper Drive project through negotiation or exercise of the City's eminent domain authority
synopsis: Authorizes the Water Bureau to acquire property rights, by negotiation or eminent domain, for a project along SW Upper Drive.

title: Authorize City Attorney to settle lawsuit related to construction of the Streetcar approach ramp located near SE 2nd Ave and accept lump sum payment in the amount of $7,500,000
synopsis: Settles the City's lawsuit over construction of the Streetcar approach ramp near SE 2nd Ave, with the City receiving a $7.5 million lump-sum payment.

title: Authorize Council to continue operating under the current City Code Chapter 3.02
synopsis: Lets Council keep operating under the current version of its procedures code (City Code Chapter 3.02).

title: Initiate two disparity studies on City contracting and workforce participation
synopsis: Starts two disparity studies on City contracting and on workforce participation.

title: Pay settlement of Adam Gregg lawsuit in the sum of $300,000 involving the Portland Police Bureau
synopsis: Pays $300,000 to settle a lawsuit involving the Portland Police Bureau.

title: Amend City Code to adopt State of Oregon Building Codes by reference (amend Code Title 24 and Sections 25.01.020, 26.01.030, and 27.01.030)
synopsis: Updates City code to adopt the State of Oregon's building codes by reference.

title: Adopt the Portland Urban Forest Plan to improve public health, build resilience to climate change, and promote environmental justice
synopsis: Adopts the Portland Urban Forest Plan, aimed at public health, climate resilience and environmental justice.

title: Denounce any attempts to deploy the United States Armed Forces, the National Guard, or militarized Federal Immigration Enforcement in Portland and establish the Protect Portland Initiative
synopsis: Denounces any deployment of the U.S. military, National Guard or militarized federal immigration enforcement in Portland, and creates the Protect Portland Initiative.

title: Add Code to enact Sanctuary City status protections (add Code Chapter 23.20)
synopsis: Writes Sanctuary City protections into City code.

title: Authorize the Bureau of Transportation to acquire certain temporary rights necessary for construction of NE 122nd Ave, Safety and Access: Beech St-Wasco St Project, through the exercise of the City’s eminent domain authority
synopsis: Authorizes the Bureau of Transportation to use eminent domain for temporary rights needed for the NE 122nd Ave Safety and Access project between Beech and Wasco streets.

title: Vacate a portion of an unnamed road near the intersection of NE 33rd Dr and NE Marine Dr subject to certain conditions and reservations (VAC-10133)
synopsis: Vacates part of an unnamed road near NE 33rd Dr and NE Marine Dr, with conditions.

title: Authorize exception to Title 17 Underground Wiring Districts Code to allow for the placement of decorative lighting across Portland Bureau of Transportation designated pedestrian plazas and the Skidmore/Old Town Historic District and the New Chinatown/Japantown Historic District (allow exception to Code Section 17.60.020)
synopsis: Makes an exception to underground wiring rules to allow decorative lighting across pedestrian plazas and the Skidmore/Old Town and New Chinatown/Japantown historic districts.

title: Amend transportation fee schedule for FY 2025-26 to reflect changes in the Plaza Use Permit program (amend TRN 3.450)
synopsis: Updates the FY 2025-26 transportation fee schedule to reflect changes to the Plaza Use Permit program.

title: Establish a charge to fund City payment of the Flood Safety Benefit Fee to the Urban Flood Safety and Water Quality District
synopsis: Creates a charge to fund the City's payment of the Flood Safety Benefit Fee to the Urban Flood Safety and Water Quality District.

title: Authorize Bureau of Transportation to acquire certain temporary rights necessary for construction of the NE Shaver Sidewalk, 102nd to 115th Avenue Project, through the exercise of the City’s Eminent Domain Authority
synopsis: Authorizes the Bureau of Transportation to use eminent domain for temporary rights needed for the NE Shaver sidewalk project from 102nd to 115th Ave.

title: Require City Administrator to develop a plan that establishes a storefront support program
synopsis: Requires the City Administrator to develop a plan for a storefront support program.

title: Adopt the Public Street Plaza Program Framework to support the creation of a permanent Public Street Plaza Program
synopsis: Adopts a framework for creating a permanent Public Street Plaza Program.

title: Amend City Code to reduce permit submittal requirements and temporarily suspend City-imposed development upgrade requirements (amend Code Chapters 11.50, 11.60, 24.85, and 33.258, and allow exception to Code Subsection 17.88.020 B.)
synopsis: Reduces permit application requirements and temporarily suspends City-imposed upgrade requirements on new development.

title: ​​Approve Comprehensive Plan Map, Zone Map, and Title 33 amendments as proposed in Portland-Gresham Urban Service Boundary Amendments Project​
synopsis: Approves Comprehensive Plan, zoning map and zoning code changes from the Portland-Gresham Urban Service Boundary Amendments Project.

title: ​​Direct City Administrator to approve Portland-Gresham Urban Services Intergovernmental Agreement
synopsis: Directs the City Administrator to approve the Portland-Gresham Urban Services intergovernmental agreement.

title: Amend Parking Space Reservation Code to allow for flexibility in the distribution of responsibilities (amend Code Section 16.20.460)
synopsis: Changes the Parking Space Reservation code to allow more flexibility in who handles which responsibilities.

title: Amend Small Donor Elections Code to adopt the recommendations of the Portland Elections Commission (amend Code Chapter 2.16)
synopsis: Updates the Small Donor Elections code to adopt the Portland Elections Commission's recommendations.

title: Reaffirm Council commitment to the Vision Zero Action Plan and convene a cross-bureau Vision Zero Task Force
synopsis: Reaffirms Council's commitment to the Vision Zero Action Plan and creates a cross-bureau Vision Zero Task Force.
